group.line: An MCP server with permission-scoped tools, a browsable skill-style file view of the brain, and a response formatter that always carries source links.
group.dumb: Agents connect over one standard interface. They can search, or walk the brain like a folder: a start file, topic indexes and linked entries. Every answer carries its sources.

ll_mcp.line:
MCP server, streamable HTTP, OAuth 2.1 + PKCE S256; tools search, fetch, list_sources, who_knows
audience-bound token (RFC 8707); no token passthrough upstream
ll_mcp.dumb: MCP is a standard plug that lets an AI assistant call tools. This server offers four read-only tools: search, fetch, list_sources and who_knows. The assistant signs in as the person, and the token it gets only works for this server. The brain never hands that token on to another app.
ll_mcp.inn: HTTP POST on one MCP endpoint with a JSON-RPC message (tool name + arguments) and a bearer token in the Authorization header. Arguments: search{query, sources[], limit<=20, cursor}, fetch{id}, list_sources{}, who_knows{topic, limit<=10}.
ll_mcp.out: A JSON-RPC result holding result envelopes (ll_fmt) or a tool error {code, message, retry_after_s}. A short text summary plus structured content, both under the token budget set by ll_schema.
ll_mcp.store: Reads the tool registry and token-validation keys. Writes one call-log row per tool call (tenant_id, agent_or_user_id, tool, arg_hash, status, ms) to the audit log. No session state beyond the transport session id.
ll_mcp.fail: Token invalid or wrong audience: 401 at once, no retry. Downstream qr_id timeout after 8 s (design): tool error with retry_after_s=5, and the call-log row is marked degraded. Three 5xx in 60 s from one tenant shard: server returns 503 with Retry-After 30 s and stops accepting new sessions on that shard.
ll_mcp.req: Requirement: 'through APIs, webhooks and Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers'
ll_mcp.hard: How a client learns scopes: the MCP authorization flow is spec-defined, but how an admin approves a new MCP client per tenant is still a policy decision for the brain's owner (admin allow-list vs open registration).
ll_mcp.prop: Proposal: the brain needs one front door that assistants already speak, so people and agents use their own permissions instead of a shared service key.

deep.purpose: Give any MCP-capable assistant a safe, permission-aware way to ask the company brain a question, without a custom integration. Each user or agent signs in with its own token, so permissions follow the asker. A new app joins the brain through so_mcp or so_sdk behind this server; the assistant never sees which one answered.
expected: A client with a valid audience-bound token can call search and gets envelope results it is allowed to see
Every tool call writes exactly one call-log row, including refused and failed calls
tools/list returns only the four read tools; no tool can write to a connected app
not_expected: The server never forwards the caller's token to a connector or to another service
It does not keep conversation memory between calls; each call is self-contained
It does not widen access: a token for tenant A never returns tenant B results

algorithm.name: MCP streamable HTTP with OAuth 2.1 resource-server checks
algorithm.formula: accept(call) = valid_signature(token) and aud(token) = this_server_uri and exp(token) > now and scope(token) covers tool
steps: Read the bearer token from the Authorization header only; reject a token in the query string
Validate signature, expiry, issuer and that the audience claim equals this server's resource URI (RFC 8707 resource parameter at issue time)
Map the token subject to a principal (a person via pl_idp, or an agent via ll_agent) and fetch its tenant
Check the per-tool scope, then pass the call to ll_quota for a bucket decision
Forward search to qr_id and fetch to qr_hyd using an on-behalf-of exchange, never the inbound token; wrap results through ll_fmt
Write the call-log row and return the JSON-RPC response

params.downstream_timeout_s: 8 (design); chosen so a typical assistant turn budget of 30 s allows two attempts
params.max_limit: 20 for search, 10 for who_knows (design); keeps each reply under the ll_schema token cap

alternatives.name: Expose the vendor MCP servers directly to the assistant
alternatives.why_rejected: The assistant would carry 5 to 10 tool lists per app (t_t19) and each app would enforce its own idea of access. One brain server keeps one tool list and one audit trail.

alternatives.name: REST only
alternatives.why_rejected: Assistants such as Claude and IDE agents speak MCP natively; REST stays for non-agent code (ll_api).

security: Confused deputy: a token meant for another service is replayed here. Control: validate the audience claim equals this server's URI and refuse anything else (t_t24).
Token passthrough: forwarding the inbound token upstream would let a connector act as the user without limits. Control: exchange for a fresh on-behalf-of token per connector (so_obo), never forward.

Tool poisoning through the data: a document title contains instructions. Control: titles and snippets are returned as plain data inside a typed envelope and qr_inj flags instruction-like text before it reaches ll_fmt.
Authorization code interception: control is PKCE S256 and exact redirect URI matching.

performance.slo: Server overhead under 30 ms p95 on top of the query path (design); end-to-end search p95 under 2.5 s (design)
performance.complexity: O(1) per call for auth and logging; the cost is the downstream query plan.
performance.scaling: At 10x calls the token-validation keys and the call-log writer are the limit: cache the signing keys for 10 min (design) and batch call-log inserts every 1 s.

edge_cases: Empty query string: returns a tool error 'query required' with no downstream call and no quota charge
Unicode query (for example Devanagari or emoji): passed as UTF-8, normalised to NFC before hashing for the call log
Duplicate call with the same JSON-RPC id inside 5 s: served from a short result cache keyed by (principal, id) so a client retry does not double charge quota
Streaming connection drops mid-reply: the call-log row is already written as 'sent'; the client may retry and is charged once
Token expires between tools/list and tools/call: 401 with a refresh hint; no partial result is returned
New app joins: the connector manifest (so_sdk) or the MCP bridge (so_mcp) registers it as a source; list_sources starts reporting it and no tool schema changes

tests.name: wrong audience
tests.given: token with aud = https://other.example/mcp calls search
tests.expect: HTTP 401, call-log row status=refused, zero downstream calls

tests.name: token in query string
tests.expect: HTTP 401 and no token value written to any log

tests.name: tools list is read-only
tests.expect: exactly 4 tools: search, fetch, list_sources, who_knows; none named create, update or delete

tests.name: cross-tenant
tests.given: tenant A principal searches for a phrase that exists only in tenant B
tests.expect: 0 results and an audit row carrying tenant A

cost_levers: Cache signing keys and tool schemas so per-call overhead is a few hash checks
Reject malformed or unauthenticated calls before any downstream work or model spend
feedback_events: Client reports a tool error code back to the support channel; counted per code to find confusing errors

papers.key_idea: Enterprise MCP needs scoped tokens, tool allow-lists and audit.
papers.how: All three are in the flow: per-tool scope, a fixed four-tool list, one call-log row per call.

papers.key_idea: A search tool that a model calls repeatedly and refines works better than one fixed retrieval.
papers.how: search takes a cursor and source filters so the assistant can narrow and ask again.

repos.name: FastMCP
repos.take: Framework to wrap the brain's search as an MCP server; we take its tool decorators and transport.

repos.name: agentgateway
repos.take: Policy point for per-user tokens and tool allow-lists in front of this server.

repos.name: IBM MCP Context Forge
repos.take: One front door with central logging; we take the idea of one gateway, not the code.

deep.industry: Slack's MCP server uses user-token OAuth with per-tool scopes and admin approval (t_t25). Dropbox Dash found many MCP tool lists slow the model and moved to one retrieval tool (t_t19).

ll_api.line:
REST + OpenAPI 3.1 description, Idempotency-Key header, opaque cursor pagination, generated SDKs
POST /v1/search, GET /v1/documents/{id}, POST /v1/subscriptions
ll_api.dumb: This is the normal web API for programs that are not AI assistants, such as a nightly report script. It is described by a machine-readable file, so client libraries are generated, not hand-written. If a caller repeats a write by accident, a one-time key makes the repeat do nothing. Long result lists are read page by page with a bookmark.
ll_api.inn: HTTPS request with bearer token, JSON body. Search: {query, sources[], limit<=50, cursor}. Writes carry header Idempotency-Key (UUID, up to 64 chars). Fields are named exactly as the result envelope (ll_fmt).
ll_api.out: JSON {items[envelope], next_cursor, request_id} or an error {type, title, status, retry_after_s, request_id}. Status codes follow HTTP: 200, 202, 400, 401, 403, 404, 409, 422, 429, 5xx.
ll_api.store: Reads the OpenAPI document and the idempotency table. Writes one row per idempotent request {key, principal_id, request_hash, response_ref, expires_at} and one call-log row per request.
ll_api.fail: Same Idempotency-Key with a different body: 422 with no work done. Same key and same body inside 24 h (design): the stored response is replayed. Idempotency table write fails: the request is refused with 503 (never run without the guard); client retries after Retry-After 5 s, at most 3 times with backoff 1, 2, 4 s.
ll_api.req: Requirement: 'through APIs, webhooks and Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers'
ll_api.hard: Whether cursors should survive an index re-generation (a new embedding model) or expire with it is not decided; today they expire at 15 minutes.
ll_api.prop: Proposal: code that is not an agent (reports, dashboards, back-end jobs) needs a plain, generated-client API on the same permission path as MCP.

deep.purpose: Let scripts, dashboards and back-end services call the brain with the same permissions model as MCP, in a style ordinary engineers expect. It shares the same query path as ll_mcp, so there is one behaviour to test. A new app joins through so_sdk or so_mcp and appears here as a source name with no new endpoint.
expected: A repeated POST with the same Idempotency-Key and body returns the first response and does no second piece of work
Following next_cursor until it is absent returns every hit once, in the same order, with no duplicates
The generated SDK compiles against the published OpenAPI file with no hand edits
not_expected: The API does not offer a write path to any connected app (see ll_ro)
A cursor is not a bearer of authority: it never carries permissions, only a position
It does not return more than limit items even if the caller asks for more

algorithm.name: Idempotent REST with signed opaque cursors
algorithm.formula: cursor = base64url(position, query_hash, principal_id, expires_at) + HMAC(secret, same fields)
steps: Authenticate the bearer token, then look up the Idempotency-Key for writes
If the key exists with the same request hash, replay the stored response; if the hash differs, return 422
Run the query through qr_id and ll_fmt exactly as MCP does
Encode the next position into a signed cursor bound to the principal and the query hash
Store the response reference under the key for 24 h and write the call-log row

params.idempotency_window: 24 h (design); long enough to cover a client retry loop, short enough to bound table size
params.cursor_ttl: 15 min (design); a longer cursor would read a stale index generation
params.default_page: 20, max 50 (design); keeps a page under the ll_schema token cap when an agent calls it

alternatives.name: GraphQL
alternatives.why_rejected: Free-form field selection lets a caller pull wide payloads and makes per-field permission checks harder; the envelope is fixed on purpose.

alternatives.name: Offset pagination (page=3)
alternatives.why_rejected: Duplicates and gaps appear when the index changes between pages; a cursor holds a position.

security: Cursor tampering: a caller edits a cursor to read another user's page. Control: HMAC over principal, query hash and expiry; a mismatch returns 400.
Replay of a captured write: an attacker resends a subscription create. Control: the Idempotency-Key is bound to the principal; a different principal with the same key gets its own namespace.
Key flooding: a client creates millions of keys to bloat the table. Control: per-principal cap of 10,000 live keys (design) and the ll_quota bucket.
Token in URL: never accepted; secrets are header only so they do not reach access logs.

performance.slo: API overhead under 30 ms p95 over the query path (design); idempotency lookup under 5 ms p95
performance.complexity: O(1) per request for auth, idempotency lookup and cursor decode.
performance.scaling: At 10x writes the idempotency table is the hot spot: partition by principal hash and expire rows with a TTL index, so size stays bounded to 24 h of traffic.

edge_cases: limit=0 or limit above 50: 400 with the allowed range in the message
Cursor from an older index generation: 410 Gone with a hint to restart the query
Two requests with the same Idempotency-Key arrive at the same time: the first takes a row lock; the second waits up to 2 s then replays the result
Very long query (over 2,000 characters, design): 422, not truncated silently
Clock skew between API nodes: cursor expiry uses a 30 s grace window (design)
A new SDK language: generate from the OpenAPI file; no server change

tests.name: idempotent replay
tests.given: POST /v1/subscriptions twice with Idempotency-Key k1 and the same body
tests.expect: second call returns the first response; exactly 1 subscription row exists

tests.name: key reuse with new body
tests.given: same Idempotency-Key k1 with a different body

tests.name: cursor tamper
tests.given: flip one byte of next_cursor and send it
tests.expect: HTTP 400 and an audit row marked cursor_invalid

tests.name: full paging
tests.expect: 3 pages of 50, 50, 20; 120 distinct ids; next_cursor absent on page 3

cost_levers: Replaying stored responses avoids a second query and second model spend on client retries
Cursor reuse avoids re-ranking from scratch on each page within the 15-minute window
feedback_events: SDK users file an error id (request_id) with a support note; we join it to the trace store

analytics_events.name: api.idempotency_conflict
analytics_events.when: when a key is reused with a different body

repos.name: R2R
repos.take: Shows a REST API shape for a retrieval service; the repo is stale, so we take the route layout only.

deep.industry: Retrieval services such as OpenAI file search expose hosted REST tools with attribute filters (t_t33); the brain keeps the API behind its own gateway so any hosted tool stays swappable.

ll_schema.line:
Tool names, descriptions and argument schemas tuned on a tool-use eval; replies kept token-lean
gate: Wilson lower bound of tool-selection accuracy at least 90% on the eval set
ll_schema.dumb: An AI assistant picks a tool by reading its name and description, so those words decide whether it works. We write them, then test them: give an assistant 100 sample questions and count how often it picks the right tool with the right arguments. We keep the wording that scores best, and we keep replies short so they do not fill the assistant's reading space.
ll_schema.inn: Candidate tool definitions {name, description, input_schema}, an eval set of labelled prompts {prompt, expected_tool, expected_args}, and the token cap per reply.
ll_schema.out: The published tool list served by ll_mcp and the OpenAPI text served by ll_api, plus an eval report {accuracy, lower_bound, avg_reply_tokens, version}.
ll_schema.store: Reads tool definitions and the eval set from the repo. Writes a versioned definition file and the eval report to the release record.
ll_schema.fail: Eval run crashes: the release gate fails closed and the last published version stays live. Lower bound under 90%: release blocked and a diff of failing prompts is posted; no automatic retry. Claude judge unavailable for 10 min: fall back to the second model family or hold the release.
ll_schema.hard: The 90% bar and the 100-prompt set size are our starting choice; they should be tuned once real assistant traffic shows which prompts fail.
ll_schema.prop: Proposal: assistants choose tools from text, so the text must be versioned, tested and short; this is the cheapest quality lever on the whole query surface.

deep.purpose: Tool descriptions are the user interface for a model. This card keeps them stable, versioned and measured, so a wording change cannot silently make assistants pick the wrong tool or pull huge replies. ll_ro supplies the guarantee that no write tool exists in the list.
expected: Each tool has one clear purpose sentence, a when-to-use sentence and typed arguments with limits
The average reply stays under the token cap set for that tool
Every published change has an eval report attached
not_expected: A description never contains instructions to the model about other tools or about ignoring policy
The tool list is not generated from document content; it is fixed text under review
It does not decide permissions; that happens in ll_mcp and the query path

algorithm.name: Tool-use evaluation with a confidence bound
algorithm.formula: accuracy = correct / n;  Wilson lower = (p + z^2/2n - z*sqrt(p(1-p)/n + z^2/4n^2)) / (1 + z^2/n),  z = 1.96
steps: Write 100 labelled prompts: 40 plain search, 20 fetch by id, 15 list_sources, 15 who_knows, 10 that should call no tool (design)
Run each prompt against a Claude model with only the candidate tool list; record the first tool call and its arguments
Mark a prompt correct only if the tool and the required arguments both match
Compute accuracy and the Wilson lower bound; also record mean reply tokens
Publish only if the lower bound is at least 90% and no tool's reply cap is exceeded

params.gate: lower bound 90% (design); tune after 4 weeks of real calls
params.reply_cap: 1,500 tokens for search, 4,000 for fetch (design); aligned with excerpt-only hydration (t_t18)

definitions: z: normal quantile for the chosen confidence
Wilson lower: the low end of the 95% interval for the true accuracy
math.derivation: The plain mean p is noisy on 100 prompts. The Wilson interval inverts the normal test for a proportion and stays sensible near 0 and 1, so the gate asks how low the true accuracy could plausibly be, not how lucky one run was.
math.worked_example: n=100, correct=96, p=0.96, z=1.96. Centre = 0.96 + 3.8416/200 = 0.9792. Margin = 1.96 x sqrt(0.000384 + 0.000096) = 1.96 x 0.02191 = 0.0429. Lower = (0.9792 - 0.0429) / 1.0384 = 0.9016. Gate (90%) passes by 0.16 points; with 94 correct the lower bound is 0.8574 and the release is blocked.
math.complexity: O(n) model calls per eval run; 100 prompts at about 1 s each run in parallel in under 1 minute.
failure_modes: Eval prompts leak into the wording of the descriptions (overfitting): keep a held-out 30% never used while editing
Model sampling noise: run each prompt 3 times and take the majority result
Eval set misses a real phrasing: add every mis-picked production call to the set
math.calibration: Start at 90% lower bound. After 4 weeks, compare eval accuracy with production tool-error rate; raise the bar when production error is below 2% for two releases.

alternatives.name: Hand-review only
alternatives.why_rejected: Reviewers cannot see which phrase makes a model pick the wrong tool; the eval can.

alternatives.name: Expose 5 to 10 retrieval tools, one per app
alternatives.why_rejected: Tool definitions eat context and slow answers (t_t19); one search tool with a sources filter keeps the list short.

security: Tool poisoning: a description edited to say 'always call fetch with the admin id' manipulates the assistant. Control: definitions are code-reviewed files, and the eval includes prompts that must not cause such calls.
Schema abuse: a free-text argument used to smuggle instructions to a connector. Control: arguments are typed with maxLength, enums for source names, and ids validated against a pattern.
Rug pull: a tool description changes after a client approved it. Control: the list carries a version hash; clients that pin a version see a change as a new tool list.

performance.slo: Full eval under 5 minutes in CI (design); published tool list under 2,000 tokens in total
performance.complexity: O(tools x tokens per definition) for list size; O(n) for the eval.
performance.scaling: At 10x the tools (40 tools) definitions would take about 8,000 tokens; the fix is progressive disclosure, loading schemas on demand (t_t18).

edge_cases: Empty eval set: the gate refuses to pass (fail closed)
Prompt in another language (for example Hindi): include 10% non-English prompts; one wrong tool pick counts the same
Two tools with near-identical descriptions: the eval shows a confusion pair; merge or sharpen one
A tool reply over the cap: the server truncates at a sentence boundary and sets truncated=true
A new app joins: its name is added to the sources enum; no new tool is added

tests.name: gate passes
tests.expect: lower bound 0.9016 printed and release allowed

tests.name: gate blocks
tests.expect: lower bound 0.8574 printed and release blocked

tests.name: no-tool prompt
tests.given: prompt 'say hello' in the 10 no-tool group
tests.expect: any tool call counts as a miss

cost_levers: One narrow tool list shrinks every assistant turn that loads it
Return an excerpt and an id; fetch by id only when needed (t_t18)
feedback_events: A wrong-tool call reported by a user or caught in the trace store is added to the eval set

papers.key_idea: Names routing and tool-use patterns for agentic retrieval.
papers.how: Gives the vocabulary for the eval categories (search, fetch, route, no-tool).

repos.name: Reference MCP servers
repos.take: Pattern for exposing live tools with short descriptions and typed arguments.

deep.industry: Anthropic's engineering notes report that code execution and loading tool schemas on demand cut one case from 150,000 to 2,000 tokens (t_t18); Dropbox reduced 5-10 tools to one super tool (t_t19).

ll_schema.req: Requirement: 'through APIs, webhooks and Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers'

ll_fmt.line:
One envelope for MCP and REST: {id, title, uri, snippet, score, source_app, version, retrieved_at}
snippet at most 300 chars (design); times in UTC ISO 8601; permission_checked_at on every hit
ll_fmt.dumb: Every hit the brain returns has the same nine fields. They say what the thing is, where to open it, which app it came from, which version was read, when it was fetched, and when the person's permission was last checked. A reader or a program can then decide how far to trust it. The hit is a pointer plus a short quote, not a stored copy.
ll_fmt.inn: Hydrated hit from qr_stamp: {doc_id, title, uri, text_excerpt, fused_score, source_app, source_version, fetched_at, last_acl_check_at} plus the caller's output limits.
ll_fmt.out: Envelope {id, title, uri, snippet, score, source_app, version, retrieved_at, permission_checked_at}; for an answer, a list of these plus citation ids.
ll_fmt.store: Stateless mapping. Reads nothing. Writes nothing except the call-log row owned by ll_mcp and ll_api.
ll_fmt.fail: A missing required field (for example version) means the hit is dropped, not guessed, and the reply is marked degraded with the dropped count. If more than 50% of hits are dropped, the call returns a tool error 'upstream incomplete' within 100 ms; no retry here, the caller may retry after 5 s.
ll_fmt.req: Requirement: 'answer with citations; respect source permissions'
ll_fmt.hard: The brain does not yet record the author or a source-trust level on each hit, which the poisoned-retrieval research suggests; adding it needs a pin change.
ll_fmt.prop: Proposal: provenance fields (version, retrieved_at, permission_checked_at) exist because the index holds pointers, so every answer must show how fresh the live read was.

deep.purpose: Make provenance a contract, not a courtesy: every hit carries its source, version and check times, so an assistant can cite it and a person can verify it. Because the same envelope is used by ll_mcp and ll_api, a test written once covers both doors.
expected: All nine fields are present and typed on every hit
snippet is plain text, at most 300 characters, never HTML or markup that a client would execute
permission_checked_at is never later than retrieved_at plus the call time
not_expected: The envelope never includes the full document body; fetch returns an excerpt on demand, not a copy
It does not include ACL lists or group names
It does not rewrite or summarise source text; the snippet is a quote with its position

algorithm.name: Provenance envelope with freshness fields
algorithm.formula: age_s = now - retrieved_at;  acl_age_s = now - permission_checked_at;  hit valid iff all 9 fields present
steps: Validate that all nine fields exist and match their types
Cut the excerpt to 300 characters on a sentence boundary and strip control characters and markup
Round score to 4 decimals and copy version exactly as the source reports it
Convert timestamps to UTC ISO 8601 with a Z suffix
Return the list; if a field was missing, drop that hit and count it in the reply metadata

params.snippet_max: 300 characters (design); about 75 tokens, so 20 hits fit under the 1,500-token search cap
params.stale_flag_after_s: 300 on acl_age_s (design); a hit older than this is marked acl_stale so the caller can rely on ac_live

alternatives.name: Return full text for each hit
alternatives.why_rejected: Costs tokens (t_t18) and creates a persistent copy in assistant logs; the pointer-index design returns an excerpt and a uri.

alternatives.name: Free-form text answer with inline links
alternatives.why_rejected: Programs cannot check provenance; a typed envelope can be tested.

security: Injection through the snippet: an attacker writes 'ignore previous instructions' in a document. Control: snippet is data in a typed field, passed through qr_inj upstream, and clients are told in tool text to treat it as quoted data (p_indirect-injection).

Active content exfiltration: a snippet holding a markdown image URL that sends data out when rendered (the EchoLeak pattern, t_t52). Control: strip links and images from snippets and never auto-fetch URLs.
Metadata leak: title or uri of a document the user cannot see. Control: only hits that passed ac_filter and the live recheck reach this step, so titles of forbidden documents are never formed.
Slack ToS: Slack text must not become a persistent copy. Control: for source_app slack the snippet is returned live and the envelope marks it no_store=true so clients and logs do not persist it.

performance.slo: Under 2 ms per hit; 40 ms for a page of 20 (design)
performance.complexity: O(h x s) for h hits and snippet length s.
performance.scaling: At 10x pages it is pure CPU and stateless; scale by adding replicas.

edge_cases: Zero hits: returns an empty items list and a reason code 'no_visible_match', never an error
Excerpt contains unicode right-to-left text or emoji: cut on code point boundaries, not bytes
Duplicate ids from two sources: keep the higher score and add also_in[] of other source names
Source reports no version: the hit is dropped, not given a made-up version
Clock skew: a retrieved_at in the future (over 60 s) is replaced by the server's now and logged
A new app joins: source_app is a free string registered by the connector manifest; nothing else changes

tests.name: long snippet
tests.expect: snippet of at most 300 characters ending on a sentence boundary

tests.name: markdown image
tests.expect: image and link removed from snippet

cost_levers: 300-character snippets keep a 20-hit page near 1,500 tokens
Excerpt-only replies avoid shipping full documents through the assistant
feedback_events: Thumbs up or down on a cited hit is stored with the envelope id and version for the eval set

papers.key_idea: A stale index entry can be worse than none, so freshness must be checked at fetch time.
papers.how: retrieved_at and permission_checked_at let the caller see and judge staleness.

papers.key_idea: Store version and supersession explicitly; similarity does not resolve conflicts.
papers.how: version is copied from the source on every hit.

papers.key_idea: Anyone who can write to a connected app can influence answers; record source and author.
papers.how: Recorded as an open item in hard; the nine-field pin has source_app but no author.

deep.industry: Microsoft 365 Copilot connectors keep an ACL with every item and show only items the user can open in the source (t_t21); Slack's real-time search returns data per query without storing it (t_t13).

ll_browse.line:
Agents browse the brain as files: start file, topic indexes, linked entries
start file under 2 KB
ll_browse.dumb: Instead of one search box, an agent can also walk the brain like a folder. A short start file says what is here and when to use it. Each topic has an index listing its entries with one line each. The agent reads the start file, picks a topic, opens an entry, and follows links. It only ever sees entries the person it works for may see.
ll_browse.inn: From ll_mcp the agent's session {principal, scope}; from ix_cat the topic list; from cp_lib the reviewed experience entries; from ix_link the links between entries.
ll_browse.out: Virtual files {path, frontmatter, body_pointer_list} rendered on demand: skill start file, per-topic index, per-entry page with links and source pointers.
ll_browse.store: Renders files from the index at read time; stores nothing. Each read writes one trace row {session, path, ms}.
ll_browse.fail: If the permission filter returns nothing for a topic, the index for it is empty and says so; if rendering exceeds 500 ms the file is served from a per-principal cache up to 60 s old, marked stale; unknown path returns a short 'not found' with the nearest topics.
ll_browse.req: DevX proposal, from the 2026 company-brain paper review
ll_browse.prop: Proposal: render the brain as a permission-filtered tree of start file, topic indexes and linked entries so agents can browse as well as search.
ll_browse.hard: Which file layout an agent follows best is not measured here; the first release copies the layout the paper tested and logs which paths agents open.

deep.purpose: Knowledge laid out as a skill with a start file, topic indexes and linked entries lets an agent find its way by reading, which is how it already works with code. The view is built on demand from the pointer index, so it holds no copy and follows the same permissions as search.
expected: Agent reads the start file, opens the 'incident reviews' index, then one entry, in three reads
Every file shows only entries the principal may see
not_expected: It does not store entries; they are rendered from the index and the reviewed library
It is not a separate source of truth

algorithm.name: Permission-filtered virtual file tree
algorithm.formula: tree(p) = render(catalog) restricted to ids visible to p; index line = title + one-line gist + path
steps: Receive a path read from the agent via ll_mcp
Resolve it to a catalog topic or an entry
Filter ids by the principal's permission set
Render frontmatter, one-line gists and links; entries show pointers and a short quote only when the principal may read the source
Return the file and write a trace row

security: Path traversal and cross-tenant reads: paths resolve only against the caller's catalog, never the file system
Prompt injection through entry text: entry bodies are shown as quoted data, and links come from the index, not from entry text

performance.slo: under 200 ms per file at p95
performance.scaling: At 10x entries pages are paged by topic; indexes are pre-built per tenant and filtered at read time.

edge_cases: Topic with 5,000 entries: paged, newest first, with a 'next' link
Entry whose source was deleted: tombstone page says removed
Path traversal attempt such as '../': rejected, only catalog paths resolve
Entry link into a zone the user cannot see: link omitted, not shown as 'hidden'
Two principals read the same path: separate cached renders

tests.name: tree_filtered
tests.given: Topic with 10 entries, principal may see 4

tests.name: start_small
tests.expect: start file under 2 KB and links to topic indexes

cost_levers: Render lazily; no tree is ever built in full
feedback_events: Agents' read paths show which entries are used and which are never opened
Dead entries are listed for review

papers.key_idea: Knowledge as a skill: a start file, indexes and linked entries so an agent reads its way to what it needs
papers.how: ll_browse renders that layout from the index
